analyst_view.overall: Early view: Alavés are winless in eight league games under Quique Sánchez Flores, whose job was already under scrutiny in October; they lost 6-1 at Barcelona before a deep-lying 0-0 at Sevilla. Deportivo (9th) are steadier under Antonio Hidalgo and have Aubameyang back from knee surgery, but they managed only five shots in their 0-0 at Espanyol.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.4 goals. Before the Sevilla draw, Alavés had scored only 5 and conceded 14 in seven games, and both teams drew 0-0 on matchday 12. Aubameyang's return gives Deportivo more threat, but he is just back from a meniscus operation and only played a half.

corners.text: The site expects 10.8 corners, 6.2 of them for Alavés. Sánchez Flores' side sat in a 3-5-2 at Sevilla and took four corners, and they have been short of attacking ideas. Neither side looks set to pin the other back for long.

cards.text: The model has 4.8 cards and I lean higher. Alavés committed 19 fouls and took three yellows at Sevilla, while Deportivo picked up four yellows at Espanyol, three of them for dangerous play. A home side short on confidence and under pressure tends to make it scrappy.

shots.text: The site expects 25.9 shots. Alavés had 9 at Sevilla and Deportivo only 5 at Espanyol, so both attacks are running cold. Deportivo's Eddahchouri (wrist) and Bright Ede are listed as doubts, which thins Hidalgo's options.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.5 on target. I lean lower because Alavés have struggled to create clear chances since September and Deportivo rarely tested Fortuño at Espanyol. Expect 6 or 7 rather than 9.
